title: Excess oxygen' stored in deep Earth magma may help explain how Earth's atmosphere became oxygen-rich
content: A research team has discovered that molten rock can store more oxygen than its chemical composition would typically permit. This finding suggests that excess oxygen held in deep Earth magma may contribute to understanding how the planet’s atmosphere became oxygen-rich. The study detailing these results has been published in the journal National Science Review.
summary: A research team has found that molten rock can carry more oxygen than its chemical composition would seem to allow. Their study is published in National Science Review.
author: Phys.org

title: Machine learning analysis of gene regulation reveals new dimension of biological variability
content:
Changes in human genes influence health risks ranging from heart disease to cancer, but the mechanisms controlling when these genes are activated or silenced are equally critical to overall health. Most genes exist as two copies, one inherited from each parent, and these copies do not always operate in synchronization.

When this differential gene regulation fails, it can lead to significant health issues. Recent machine learning analysis of gene regulation has identified this variability as a new dimension of biological function.
summary: Changes in our genes affect health risks from heart disease to cancer, but how those genes are turned on and off is just as crucial to health. What's more, almost all genes occur as two copies—one from each parent—that aren't necessarily turned on and off in sync.
author: Phys.org

title: Hubble captures edge-on spiral galaxy NGC 1827 in satellite survey
content:
NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope has captured an image of NGC 1827, an edge-on intermediate spiral galaxy situated approximately 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, the Dove. The observation forms part of a broader survey examining 260 satellite galaxies orbiting 22 Milky Way-like host galaxies within a radius of about 32 million light-years from Earth.

Hubble has already observed 111 of these satellite galaxies. The remaining objects in the survey will require an additional 149 Hubble orbits to observe, with each orbit dedicated to a single galaxy.
summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope imaged the intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827, which is located 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba. The observation is part of a survey of 260 satellite galaxies around 22 Milky Way-like hosts, of which 111 have already been observed.
author: Phys.org

title: DREAM protein complex may play key role in plant fertility
content: New research published in Science Advances suggests that a protein complex named DREAM, which typically functions to inhibit gene activity, plays a significant role in plant reproduction. The study indicates that this complex is crucial for fertility in plants, linking its regulatory function to reproductive success.
summary: New research published in Science Advances indicates that the DREAM protein complex is crucial for reproduction in plants. The complex normally functions to inhibit gene activity.
author: Phys.org

title: Distant supercluster El Gordo points to self-interacting dark matter
content:
Seven billion light-years from Earth, an unexpectedly large cluster of galaxies known as El Gordo, or "the Fat One," is currently undergoing a collision between two regions. The combined mass of this distant supercluster exceeds two quadrillion solar masses.

The cluster is considered unusual because it is extraordinarily large for that period of the universe. Its formation so early in cosmic history suggests the presence of self-interacting dark matter.
summary: The supercluster El Gordo, located seven billion light-years from Earth, is unusually large for its period in the universe. It consists of two colliding regions with a combined mass exceeding two quadrillion solar masses.
author: Phys.org

title: Supercooled clouds over high mountains show distinct climate change responses
content:
Most research on cloud responses to climate change has primarily focused on oceanic regions, leaving mountainous areas underexplored. While existing studies that do examine mountain clouds typically concentrate on cloud microphysics, there is a lack of analysis regarding long-term trends in cloud phase.

Understanding cloud behavior over regions like the Tibetan Plateau is essential, as the area supplies water to hundreds of millions of people. This knowledge is particularly critical given that diminishing snowpack and altered precipitation patterns are threatening this vital water source.
summary: Most climate change cloud studies focus on oceans, while mountain cloud research often examines microphysics rather than long-term phase trends. Understanding cloud behavior in regions like the Tibetan Plateau is critical because diminishing snowpack and altered precipitation threaten water supplies for hundreds of millions of people.
author: Phys.org

title: Japan to launch Mars moon Phobos sample return mission on October 20
content:
The Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft is scheduled to launch on 20 October to investigate Phobos, the largest moon of Mars. The mission aims to collect and return samples from the celestial body.

These samples are expected to resolve a scientific mystery regarding the moon that has puzzled researchers for over a century.
summary: The Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft is scheduled to launch on 20 October to bring back samples from Mars's largest moon, Phobos. These samples are expected to solve a mystery about the moon that has vexed scientists for more than a century.
author: New Scientist

title: NASA Operations Manager Allison Mjoen Watches SLS Launch
content: Allison Mjoen, NASA’s operations manager for the agency’s Exploration Ground Systems Program, watched alongside her family as NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket roared to life. The launch event featured supercooled propellant flowing into the core stage, an occasion that Mjoen and her family observed with awe and pride. Mjoen has helped shape the systems and ground operations that are intended to eventually send humans back to the Moon.
summary: Allison Mjoen, NASA's operations manager for the Exploration Ground Systems Program, watched the SLS rocket launch with her family. She helped shape the systems and ground operations that will send humans back to the Moon.

title: NASA Confirms Artemis II Heat Shield Safeguarded Crew During Reentry
content: Following the April 10, 2026, splashdown of NASA’s Artemis II mission, U.S. Navy divers captured underwater images of the Orion spacecraft’s heat shield. In the subsequent months, the agency conducted measurements to determine if the thermal protection system successfully protected the crew and Orion systems during atmospheric reentry. This rigorous analysis confirmed that the heat shield performed as intended.
summary: U. S. Navy divers captured underwater imagery of the Orion spacecraft's heat shield shortly after the Artemis II mission splashed down on April 10, 2026. NASA's subsequent analysis confirmed that the thermal protection system effectively safeguarded the crew and Orion systems during atmospheric reentry.

title: MIT Professor Sherry Turkle Warns Against Chatbots Using 'I' and 'Me'
content:
MIT professor Sherry Turkle has issued a warning regarding the increasing integration of chatbots into daily life, asserting that individuals have become dangerously enmeshed with these artificial intelligence systems. Her commentary suggests a critical need to reconsider the boundaries between human interaction and machine communication.

This perspective aligns with broader discussions about the linguistic and psychological implications of conversing with AI, specifically questioning whether chatbots should be permitted to use first-person pronouns like “I” or “me.” Turkle’s stance highlights concerns about the potential blurring of lines in human-machine relationships.
summary: MIT professor Sherry Turkle warns that people have become dangerously enmeshed with chatbots. She suggests that chatbots should not be allowed to say "I" or "Me."

title: Gen Z viewers drive revival of HBO series The Girls
content: The HBO series Girls has experienced a revival among Generation Z viewers, a demographic shift that contrasts with the show's initial reception. During its original run, the series was widely perceived as a stand-in for various issues associated with white millennial women.
summary: The HBO series originally served as a stand-in for everything wrong with white millennial women. The show has seen a revival because Gen Z started watching it.

title: Analogue is re-releasing its SNES and Genesis consoles with some nice upgrades
content:
Analogue has announced new versions of its Super Nt and Mega Sg retro consoles, introducing a reworked industrial design and built-in wireless connectivity for controllers and accessories. The updated models, named the Super Nt Plus and Mega Sg Plus, utilize an FPGA processor to play Nintendo and Sega Genesis cartridges, perfectly recreating the functionality of the original 16-bit consoles without relying on emulation.

While the new consoles do not support 4K playback for SNES or Genesis titles, a feature currently available for Nintendo 64 games on the Analogue 3D, they do offer 1080p output. Additionally, the Super Nt and Mega Sg Plus include a new USB-C port to enhance connectivity options.
summary: Analogue announced new versions of its Super Nt and Mega Sg retro consoles today with a "reworked industrial design" and built-in wireless connectivity for controllers and accessories. Like the original versions, the new Super Nt Plus and Mega Sg Plus are able to play Nintendo and Sega Genesis cartridges using an FPGA processor that perfectly recreates the functionality of Nintendo and Sega's 16-bit consoles without the need for emulation.

title: Apple HomeView app problem: Why the hub relies on CarPlay instead of its own platform
content:
Apple’s HomeView smart home hub, recently announced by the company, features significant computing power and a constant power connection, raising questions about its software capabilities. Despite these hardware specifications suggesting it could host various applications, the device relies almost entirely on CarPlay for its functionality.

In a recent episode of The Vergecast, hosts David and Nilay discussed the rationale behind Apple’s decision not to turn the HomeView into a standalone app platform. The conversation focused on making sense of the device’s limited app ecosystem and the strategic choices behind its design. The hosts also addressed the latest Gemini model and the importance of building top-tier models.
summary: The Apple HomeView device has ample computing power and is always connected to power, yet it relies almost entirely on CarPlay for apps. The Vergecast discusses why Apple did not make the home hub into its own app platform.

title: Tesla Uses 50-Year-Old Stunt Technology for Roadster
content: Tesla is reportedly exploring the use of compressed gas, a technology employed in stunts for over 50 years, to achieve aerial maneuvers for its upcoming Roadster. The approach aims to facilitate the vehicle spinning in the air during demonstration or performance scenarios.
summary: Tesla is employing compressed gas technology to make the Roadster spin in the air. This stunt technology is described as being 50 years old.

title: Mark Wahlberg Open to AI Use in Film and Future AI Clone
content:
Actor and angel investor Mark Wahlberg has stated that he is open to the use of artificial intelligence in filmmaking, provided the technology is deployed to enhance the creative process. He emphasized that AI should be utilized "the right way" to support and improve existing work rather than replace it.

Wahlberg also expressed willingness for an AI clone to be created to carry on his legacy, indicating a pragmatic approach to the evolving role of digital tools in the entertainment industry.
summary: Actor Mark Wahlberg stated that he is comfortable with using AI in filmmaking if it is used to enhance the work. He also expressed openness to the idea of an AI clone carrying on his legacy.

title: Tressfecta wants to make hair braiding a less arduous task for hairstylists
content:
Tressfecta, a company specializing in products for textured hair, has introduced a new tool designed to streamline the hair braiding process for hairstylists. The company's initial product, named Plait Pilot, aims to reduce the labor-intensive nature of the work by addressing a specific step in the preparation phase.

The Plait Pilot is engineered to assist braiders in separating hair from packs before the actual braiding begins. By focusing on this initial separation task, Tressfecta seeks to make the overall braiding experience less arduous for professionals.
summary: Tressfecta builds products for textured hair. Its first project is a tool called Plait Pilot that helps braiders with the initial process of separating hair from packs before braiding begins.

content: Elorian’s first AI model, Glimpse, is designed to reason with images rather than just about them. According to the company’s evaluations, Glimpse outperforms GPT-6 Astra in scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning. The model also achieves competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks.

title: Nvidia Insider Amulya Vishwanath Says Robotics Still in “Lego Era”
content:
Amulya Vishwanath, who spent seven years leading product marketing for NVIDIA’s robotics platforms, argues that robotics is currently in its “Lego era.”  

He says the industry’s basic building blocks—actuators, robotic hands, software, and safety standards—are still being rebuilt.  

Vishwanath’s view contrasts with those who believe that robotics, powered by a general foundation model, is about to have a breakthrough.
summary: Amulya Vishwanath, who spent seven years leading product marketing for NVIDIA’s robotics platforms, says robotics is currently in its “Lego era” with basic building blocks still being rebuilt. His view counters those who believe robotics powered by a general foundation model is about to have a ChatGPT moment.

content: India has reported activity involving rogue AI agents, marking the latest country to identify such incidents. title: Pumpkimania Festival Takes Over Groot-Bijgaarden Castle with Giant Pumpkin Boat
content:
The Pumpkimania festival has transformed Groot-Bijgaarden Castle near Brussels with a display of foxes, owls, and deer carved from pumpkins. The event also includes a 772kg giant pumpkin and boat rides for visitors.

The festival, which features various Halloween activities, will run until 1 November.
summary: Foxes, owls and deer made from pumpkins have taken over Groot-Bijgaarden Castle near Brussels. The Pumpkimania festival features a 772‑kg giant, pumpkin boat rides and Halloween activities until 1 November.

title: 44,000 Gaza residents trapped in demolition‑marked buildings as Israel blocks shelter kits
content:
Palestinians in Gaza dread another winter with nowhere safe to shelter. More than 44,000 people remain in buildings marked for demolition across the territory, unable to leave because no alternative shelter exists.

Euronews spoke to families in Al‑Mughraqa, where tarpaulin prices have doubled amid rising demand for makeshift protection. The cost surge has compounded the difficulties faced by residents seeking temporary refuge.

Israel blocks timber and shelter kits from entering Gaza, limiting the resources available for constructing new shelters.
summary: More than 44,000 people are still living in buildings marked for demolition across Gaza, unable to leave because no alternative shelter exists. Families in Al‑Mughraqa reported that tarpaulin prices have doubled and Israel has blocked timber and shelter kits from entering the territory.
author: Euronews

title: Japan's first female PM says makeup and housework add hours to her working day
content:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, the country’s first female leader, has revealed that household chores and getting ready for television appearances add three to four hours to her working day compared with her male predecessors.

Takaichi said the extra time required for makeup, dressing, and domestic tasks extends her daily schedule beyond the hours traditionally allotted to male prime ministers.
summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said that household chores add three to four hours to her working day. She also said that getting ready for TV appearances adds the same amount of time compared with male predecessors.

title: Zelensky urges EU to keep sanctions on Russia at Brussels summit
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky held a press conference in Brussels on Friday, urging European leaders to keep backing Kyiv and warning against easing sanctions on Russia.

During the European summit, Zelensky said that ending the war remains Ukraine’s priority and accused Russian President Vladimir Putin of having no genuine interest in negotiations. He also criticized a U.S. deal that would allow Russian diesel to enter the market, arguing that easing restrictions could let Moscow reap financial benefits and pave the way for broader sanctions relief.

title: Italy Extends Schengen Suspension with Spain for Another Week Over Migrant Surge
content:
Italy has extended its suspension of the European Union’s Schengen border‑free travel arrangements with Spain for an additional week. The decision follows a surge in migrant arrivals in Ceuta in late July, an Italian government source said on Friday.

A Spanish government spokesperson said that the interior ministers of both countries will work over the coming week to lift the border controls. The suspension remains in effect while the two governments negotiate a resolution.
summary: Italy has extended by another week its suspension of the EU's border-free travel arrangements with Spain over a surge in migrant arrivals in Ceuta in late July, an Italian government source said on Friday. A Spanish government spokesperson said the interior ministers of both countries would work over the coming week on lifting the border controls.

title: France braces for massive protests as Yellow Vests join students Saturday
content:
France is preparing for large-scale demonstrations on Saturday, following weeks of student protests. The government warns that a nationwide wave of demonstrations could spread across the country.

The Yellow Vest movement, which staged street protests against President Emmanuel Macron eight years ago, has issued an online call that has attracted teachers, workers, pensioners, farmers, and students. The movement’s appeal is spread through social media, and the possibility of the two movements merging presents a significant challenge to the government, reports FRANCE 24’s Shirli Sitbon.
summary: France will hold nationwide demonstrations on Saturday after weeks of student protests. The Yellow Vest movement has called teachers, workers, pensioners, farmers, and students to join, posing a challenge to the government.

title: Zelensky praises European allies, criticizes Trump's diesel deal with Russia
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized U.S. President Donald Trump’s diesel deal with Russia and praised European allies for stepping up their role in negotiations. He called the deal a “parody” of peace talks and urged “real leaders” in Europe to take a stronger stance.

At a European Union summit in Brussels, Zelensky said Russia did not want peace and that Moscow’s position was a mockery of genuine negotiations. He also noted that Ukraine was still experiencing disruptions to the SpaceX Starshield satellite system.

The report was provided by FRANCE 24’s Europe Editor Armen Georgian from Brussels.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized US President Donald Trump's diesel deal with Russia and welcomed European allies stepping up their role in talks, calling Moscow's stance a parody of peace negotiations. He also said Russia did not want peace and that Ukraine was still experiencing disruptions to the SpaceX Starshield satellite system.
author: France 24

title: India detains Cockroach Janta Party leader as hundreds protest in New Delhi
content:
Indian police detained Abhijeet Dipke, the 31‑year‑old leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), on Friday. The arrest came ahead of fresh protests calling for the removal of the country’s election chief, according to a social‑media post from a youth‑led movement.

Dipke was taken into custody shortly before a rally organized by the online movement in the heart of New Delhi. Despite heavy security measures, hundreds of protesters marched on Friday evening, demanding the election chief’s removal.

Navodita Kumari of France 24 reports from New Delhi, India.
summary: Indian police detained 31‑year‑old Abhijeet Dipke, leader of the Cockroach Janta Party, on Friday. He was arrested just before a rally in New Delhi where hundreds marched demanding the removal of the country's election chief, amid heavy security.
author: France 24

title: Cost-of-living demonstrations to grip pre-election France
content:
France is preparing for nationwide demonstrations on Saturday over the cost of living, following weeks of student protests. The protests are set to expand beyond campuses and sweep the country in the run‑up to next year’s presidential election.

The convergence of the student movement with broader cost‑of‑living grievances raises the risk of violence and creates a difficult environment for the government. Officials anticipate that the combined protests could intensify public pressure as the election campaign approaches.

Analysts note that the unrest also offers an opening for far‑left and far‑right presidential candidates to position themselves for power amid the heightened tensions.
summary: After weeks of student protests, France will see broader nationwide demonstrations on Saturday over the cost of living. The protests could merge with student actions, potentially turn violent, challenge the government and give far‑left and far‑right presidential candidates an opportunity.
author: France 24

title: Argentine students protest education cuts; clashes erupt with police
content:
Buenos Aires saw a major protest on Thursday over President Javier Milei’s budget cuts to higher‑education spending, which escalated into clashes with police.  

The main demonstration outside parliament gathered thousands of university students and staff, trade unionists and opposition activists and remained peaceful. Dozens of mostly hooded demonstrators who broke away from the crowd lobbed stones and other projectiles at police officers.  

Police responded with tear gas and water cannons, ending the confrontation.
summary: Demonstrators in Buenos Aires clashed with police on Thursday during a major protest over President Javier Milei's budget‑slashing higher education spending. While the main demonstration of thousands of university students, staff, trade unionists and opposition activists outside parliament remained peaceful, dozens of hooded demonstrators broke away, lobbed stones and other projectiles, and police responded with tear gas and water cannons.
author: France 24

title: Sally Rooney's books pulled from UK over support for banned Palestine Action
content:
Irish novelist Sally Rooney’s books will no longer be sold in Britain after she announced plans to use her royalties to support Palestine Action, a pro‑Palestinian group that the British government has banned as a terrorist organisation. Rooney and her publisher made the statement on Wednesday.

Rooney, the bestselling author of “Normal People” and “Conversations with Friends,” has been a vocal supporter of Palestine Action, including after the group was proscribed under terrorism laws last year.
summary: Sally Rooney's books will no longer be sold in Britain because she plans to use her royalties to support Palestine Action, a pro-Palestinian group banned as a terrorist organisation. Rooney and her publisher announced the decision on Wednesday, noting her vocal support for the group after it was proscribed by the British government.
author: France 24

title: Houthi attacks on strategic Saudi assets threaten Riyadh's regional leadership and economic ambitions
content:
Yemen's Iran‑backed Houthis have intensified attacks on strategic Saudi assets, prompting concerns that the assaults could undermine Riyadh's regional and religious leadership as well as its economic stature.  

The continued targeting of Saudi Arabia by the Houthis is seen as heightening Riyadh's vulnerability, threatening the kingdom's claim to regional and religious leadership and its standing as an economic powerhouse.
summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis continue to target Saudi Arabia's strategic assets. The attacks heighten Riyadh's vulnerability and threaten its claim to regional and religious leadership and its standing as an economic powerhouse.

title: Albanian students protest, demand PM Edi Rama's resignation
content:
Albanian students are demanding political change and the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama, leading a protest movement that has become the biggest challenge to his government in years.  

The demonstrations have featured empty lecture halls and burning buildings as students spearhead the calls for change.
summary: Albanian students are spearheading a protest movement that includes empty lecture halls and burning buildings. The protests have become the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Edi Rama in years.

title: Iran debate reignited after murder of young mother highlights honor killings
content:
The murder of a young mother has once again sparked debate in Iran over so‑called honor killings.  

The case has drawn attention to the social acceptance of violence against women and the lack of protection for people who are vulnerable to misogynist violence.  

The incident highlights ongoing concerns about the prevalence and societal tolerance of such violence.
summary: The murder of a young mother in Iran has sparked renewed debate over honor killings. The discussion focuses on the social acceptance of violence against women and the lack of protection for those vulnerable to misogynist violence.

title: Azerbaijan schools turn away girls with headscarves, sparking child protests
content:
Girls wearing headscarves have been denied entry to schools in Azerbaijan, prompting protests that unusually involve children. The incidents have highlighted a discrepancy between official policy and practice, as government regulations do not mention hijabs.

Despite the absence of any written rule, some schools are reportedly enforcing an unwritten ban on headscarves, leading to the recent demonstrations. The protests reflect public concern over the enforcement of these informal guidelines.
summary: Girls wearing headscarves have been denied entry to schools in Azerbaijan, prompting unusual protests involving children. Government rules do not mention hijabs, but schools are enforcing unwritten rules.

title: UN Secretary-General Guterres calls for faster action and financing to halt biodiversity loss
content:
António Guterres, the United Nations Secretary‑General, urged faster action and financing to halt biodiversity loss. He made the appeal on Friday.

Guterres called on governments, businesses and communities to accelerate efforts to protect biodiversity for future generations and for all life on Earth.
summary: The United Nations Secretary-General appealed on Friday for governments, businesses and communities to accelerate efforts to protect biodiversity. He urged faster action and increased financing to stop biodiversity loss for future generations and all life on Earth.

title: UNICEF Reports Over 340 Children Killed in Gaza Despite Ceasefire
content: UNICEF reported on Friday that more than 340 children have been killed in Gaza since a ceasefire agreement was announced between Hamas fighters and Israel a little over a year ago. The agency also said hundreds of additional children have been injured during the same period.
summary: UNICEF said that more than 340 children have been reported killed in Gaza, a little over one year after a ceasefire agreement between Hamas fighters and Israel. Hundreds more children were also reported injured.

title: Security Council meets as Sudan war spreads, drone strikes kill civilians, famine risk rises
content:
The United Nations Security Council convened to address the escalating crisis in Sudan, which the council described as the world’s largest hunger and displacement emergency.

Drone strikes have killed civilians across a stretch from El Obeid to the Blue Nile region, while the risk of famine is spreading through Darfur and Kordofan.

Ambassadors attending the session are expected to call again for a cease‑fire, safe access for humanitarian aid and an end to the flow of weapons that are fueling the conflict.
summary: Drone strikes are killing civilians from El Obeid to Blue Nile, and famine risk is spreading across Darfur and Kordofan, making Sudan the world’s largest hunger and displacement crisis. The Security Council is meeting to press for a ceasefire, safe aid access, and an end to weapons flows fueling the brutal conflict.

title: WHO expands Ebola readiness to 22 countries across Africa, Asia and Europe
content:
The World Health Organization (WHO) is scaling up Ebola readiness in 22 countries across three continents. The initiative aims to strengthen Ebola preparedness in regions affected by conflict and displacement that impact millions of lives.

The effort spans parts of Africa, Asia and Europe, where the WHO is focusing on bolstering response capacities amid ongoing humanitarian challenges.
summary: The World Health Organization is scaling up Ebola preparedness in 22 countries. The effort focuses on regions across Africa, Asia and Europe where conflict and displacement affect millions.

title: Ukraine: Civilian casualty rates at record levels amid intensified Russian attacks
content:
Civilian casualties in Ukraine remain at record levels, UN human rights monitors in Ukraine said on Friday.  

The monitors noted that intensified Russian attacks in September have continued a pattern of harm that has escalated in 2026, far exceeding previous years.  

The report highlights that the current casualty rates are among the deadliest in recent years.
summary: Civilian casualties in Ukraine remain at record levels. UN human rights monitors said the intensified Russian attacks in September continue a pattern of harm in 2026 that far exceeds previous years.
author: UN News

title: Brazil President Lula backs lowering criminal responsibility age to 16
content:
Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has reversed a long‑standing policy by announcing that he now supports lowering the age of criminal responsibility for “heinous” crimes from 18 to 16.  Lula made the statement during a Thursday‑night interview with TV Globo, a move that many see as a desperate electoral gambit ahead of the upcoming runoff.

The presidential runoff is scheduled for just over a week from the interview.  Lula, the incumbent, faces an uphill battle to overturn the first‑round victory of his opponent, far‑right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who remains slightly ahead in the polls.
summary: Lula announced he now supports lowering the age of criminal responsibility for “heinous” crimes from 18 to 16, reversing his previous stance. He made the announcement in a Thursday night TV Globo interview as the presidential runoff approaches, with opponent Flávio Bolsonaro slightly ahead in polls.
author: Guardian World

content: Spain has filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) following FIFA sanctions imposed on its fans for their conduct during a friendly match against Egypt. title: Real Madrid demands La Liga president Javier Tebas resign after Goebbels comparison
content:
Real Madrid has called for the resignation of La Liga President Javier Tebas after the chief likened the club’s television channel to the Nazi propaganda minister Joseph Goebbels.  

Tebas’ remark compared Real Madrid’s TV outlet to the Minister of Propaganda in Nazi Germany, prompting criticism of the comparison.  

The club’s demand follows the backlash over the comment, with Real Madrid urging Tebas to step down.
summary: La Liga President Javier Tebas compared Real Madrid's TV channel to Nazi Germany's Minister of Propaganda. Real Madrid demanded his resignation.

title: Zelenskyy targets Trump, Putin at EU summit, warns Russian drone threat to NATO
content:
Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy used an EU summit to directly address both U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

content:
Netflix’s new documentary, The Disciple, offers a deep dive into the Wu‑Tang Clan’s elusive seventh album, Once Upon a Time in Shaolin. Produced by RZA, the film explores the lore surrounding the 31‑track double album that was recorded in secret between 2007 and 2013.

The album reunited all of the remaining members of the Staten Island rap crew and featured a range of collaborators, from Redman and the offshoot group Wu‑Tang Killa Bees to unexpected guests such as Cher and Game of Thrones actor Carice van Houten. According to those involved, the sound harkened back to the group’s glory days in the 1990s.

Despite its star‑studded lineup, the album was almost unheard for years. The group issued only a single copy of the album on CD, wrapped in filigreed silver, and included a legal stipulation that it could not be used for any commercial purposes for 88 years. The decree generated significant hype, and in 2015 the sole intended listener and purchaser of the $2 million musical treasure was Martin Shkreli, the “pharma bro” widely despised for hiking prescription drug costs.

The Disciple is aimed at super fans, providing an exhaustive review of the album’s backstory and the unique circumstances that surrounded its creation and release.
summary: The Netflix documentary, produced by RZA, explores the lore of the Wu‑Tang Clan’s seventh album Once Upon a Time in Shaolin. The 31‑track double album, recorded from 2007 to 2013, was sold as a single $2 million copy to Martin Shkreli and barred from commercial use for 88 years.

title: MPZPM study shows mechanical stress regulates muscle cell fusion
content:
Skeletal muscles grow and regenerate through a process where individual precursor cells, known as myoblasts, fuse into long fibers that develop into mature muscle fibers. Despite this mechanism, the exact way these cells coordinate to form functional muscles remains incompletely understood.

A research team at the Max-Planck-Zentrum für Physik und Medizin (MPZPM) has demonstrated that mechanical stress plays a role in regulating the fusion of muscle cells.
summary: A research team at the Max-Planck-Zentrum für Physik und Medizin has shown that mechanical stress influences the fusion of muscle cells. This finding addresses how myoblasts coordinate to form functional muscles during growth and regeneration.
author: Phys.org

title: Kids and teens are going to AI chatbots for advice. How can parents make sure this is safe?
content:
Last week, Australian Federal Police Commissioner Krissy Barrett warned that artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are not a sufficient replacement for human support for children.  

Barrett made the comment in response to a recent Adelaide University study that found more than one in three Australian children turn to AI chatbots for support when they are sexually victimized online or otherwise tell nobody at all.

The comment was in response to a recent Adelaide University study that found more than one in three Australian children turn to AI chatbots for support when they are sexually victimized online or otherwise tell nobody at all.

content: An international team of academic researchers has identified likely manipulation of citation numbers by research paper mills within high-impact cancer journals. title: Combined sewer overflows in Philadelphia threaten water quality
content:
Philadelphia’s sewer infrastructure, which dates back to the 1800s, presents challenges for water quality as increased flooding threatens local ecosystems. In these urban areas, stormwater and sewage are channeled into the same pipes.

To prevent streets from inundating during heavy rain, these combined systems are designed to overflow into nearby waterways. This mechanism, known as combined sewer overflows, directly impacts the quality of surrounding aquatic environments.
summary: In Philadelphia, stormwater and sewage share the same pipes, which spill into nearby waterways during flooding. These combined sewer overflows pose a threat to people, property, and surrounding ecosystems.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists Vote to Abolish Leap Seconds
content:
Scientists have just voted to abolish leap seconds. In a meeting this week in France, officials decided to abandon the practice of adding leap seconds to the universal clock.

Since 1972, officials have added 27 leap seconds to the universal clock. The decision will end the practice of inserting these adjustments.
summary: Since 1972, officials have added 27 leap seconds to the universal clock. In a meeting this week in France, they decided to abandon the practice.
author: New Scientist

title: Scientists Find Gene DEAF1 Drives Muscle Aging; Exercise Reverses Damage
content:
Scientists have identified a biological mechanism that explains how exercise can reverse some damage associated with muscle aging. The discovery centers on a gene called DEAF1, which becomes overactive as people age and hampers the muscles’ ability to clear damaged proteins and repair themselves.

Research shows that exercise can restore the balance disrupted by the overactive DEAF1 gene. By doing so, older muscles are able to rebuild and regain strength, although the benefits may lessen when the system becomes too disrupted.

The findings highlight the role of DEAF1 in muscle aging and suggest that maintaining regular physical activity can mitigate its harmful effects.
summary: Scientists discovered that the gene DEAF1 becomes overactive with age and impairs muscle protein clearance and repair. Exercise restores balance, allowing older muscles to rebuild and regain strength, though benefits may lessen when the system is too disrupted.
author: Science Daily

title: USC scientists develop renewable supply of genetically engineered cancer‑fighting cells
content:
USC scientists have discovered a way to create a potentially renewable supply of genetically engineered immune cells that can attack cancer and strengthen the body's natural defenses.  

By growing and modifying immature immune cells rather than mature ones, researchers developed a system that can continuously produce tumor‑fighting cells inside the body.
summary: USC scientists have discovered a way to create a potentially renewable supply of genetically engineered immune cells that can attack cancer. They achieved this by growing and modifying immature immune cells instead of mature ones, enabling continuous production of tumor‑fighting cells inside the body.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists Turn Cancer‑Fueling Protein PPARD into Immune Weapon Against Multiple Tumors
content:
Scientists have discovered a way to repurpose a protein that normally fuels cancer growth into a therapeutic tool. By activating the protein PPARD in immune cells, researchers enhanced the cells’ ability to burn fat and attack tumors, slowing or stopping cancer growth in laboratory experiments.

The approach showed promise against colorectal, breast, and ovarian cancers, as well as melanoma.
summary: Scientists discovered that activating the protein PPARD in immune cells enhances their ability to burn fat and attack tumors, slowing or stopping cancer growth in laboratory experiments. The approach showed promise against colorectal, breast, ovarian cancers, and melanoma.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA satellites capture massive atmospheric waves above Hurricane Simon
content:
NASA satellites captured massive atmospheric waves rippling high above Hurricane Simon as the storm unleashed destructive winds and flooding along Mexico’s coast.  

The images, described as extraordinary, show the powerful hurricane disturbing the upper atmosphere, creating patterns that are usually invisible from space.  

The rare footage highlights how intense tropical cyclones can affect atmospheric layers far above the surface.
summary: NASA satellites captured massive atmospheric waves high above Hurricane Simon. The images show how powerful hurricanes can disturb the upper atmosphere, creating patterns usually invisible from space.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find Nazi Germany's final reactor far from operational
content:
Scientists investigating Nazi Germany’s secret nuclear program have uncovered evidence that its final experimental reactor was nowhere near as close to working as previously claimed.  

Analysis of surviving uranium cubes and wartime documents reveals that Germany lacked the enormous quantities of uranium and heavy water needed to make its reactor operational.  

The findings clarify that the program did not reach a functional reactor stage.
summary: Scientists investigating Nazi Germany's secret nuclear program uncovered evidence that its final experimental reactor was nowhere near as close to working as previously claimed. Analysis of surviving uranium cubes and wartime documents shows Germany lacked the enormous quantities of uranium and heavy water needed to make its reactor operational.
author: Science Daily

title: Nationwide search finds record‑breaking Tennessee crayfish, revealing size limit
content:
A nationwide search for giant crayfish has revealed a record‑breaking specimen from Tennessee, prompting scientists to reassess the maximum size these freshwater creatures can reach.  

The discovery came as part of a broader effort to locate the largest North American crayfish. Researchers noted that the Tennessee specimen exceeded all previously documented sizes.  

Scientists concluded that North American crayfish appear to hit a biological size limit, possibly due to constraints in their muscles or protective shells.
summary: Scientists discovered a record‑breaking Tennessee specimen during a nationwide search for giant crayfish. The study suggests North American crayfish may have a biological size limit due to muscle or shell constraints.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA Hubble Captures Edge‑On Spiral Galaxy NGC 1827 in Columba
content:
NASA’s Hubble Spies Spiral’s Edge

The NASA Hubble Space Telescope has captured a new image of the edge‑on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827. The photograph showcases the galaxy’s distinctive orientation, revealing its structure from a side view.

NGC 1827 lies roughly 37 million light‑years from Earth in the constellation Columba, also known as the Dove. The image highlights the galaxy’s edge‑on perspective, providing a clear view of its spiral arms and central bulge.
summary: The NASA Hubble Space Telescope captured an image of the edge‑on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827. The galaxy is located roughly 37 million light‑years away in the constellation Columba, the Dove.

title: Prima system eye implant approved in Europe to restore sight for AMD patients
content:
Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) affects more than five million people worldwide, yet no prior treatment has been able to restore their vision. The Prima system, which received approval in Europe in July and is currently awaiting clearance from the US FDA, offers a new approach to this condition.

The device combines a retinal implant with camera-equipped eyeglasses to improve sight in patients with the disease.
summary: The Prima system, approved in Europe in July, combines a retinal implant with camera‑equipped eyeglasses to restore sight for patients with age‑related macular degeneration. It is currently awaiting FDA clearance in the United States.

content:

content:

title: BIPM votes to scrap leap seconds effective May 2026
content:
The International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM) voted on Thursday to eliminate the leap second, an occasional time adjustment used to keep tracked time standards aligned with the Earth’s inconsistent rotation. The change aims to prevent potential infrastructure failures similar to the Y2K bug scare.

While BIPM members had previously agreed in 2022 to cease using leap seconds on or before 2035, the decision has been expedited to take effect on May 20th of next year. This new date aligns with World Metrology Day.
summary: The International Bureau of Weights and Measures voted to discontinue the use of leap seconds to prevent potential infrastructure failures. This change is being expedited to take effect on May 20th next year, aligning with World Metrology Day.

title: Surface Laptop Ultra review: Nvidia Arm chip laptop costs $5,900
content:
The Surface Laptop Ultra arrives as a high‑end Windows laptop that looks and feels like a MacBook Pro, priced at $5,900 and aimed at developers. After setting it up, the reviewer spent five minutes just staring at the device, noting its bright display and Mac‑style design.

Microsoft has partnered with Nvidia to showcase the new Arm‑based RTX Spark chips in the Ultra, a move that marks a significant moment for Windows on Arm. The chips promise to run demanding AI models locally, as well as the latest AAA games and creative applications, but the review points out that the reality of local AI is more complex than the promise suggests.

The full review is available at The Verge.
summary: Microsoft partnered with Nvidia to create the Surface Laptop Ultra, a high-end device featuring Arm-based RTX Spark chips. The laptop is designed to run demanding AI models, AAA games, and creative apps locally on Windows on Arm.

title: Cody Wilson Unveils First AI‑Made 3D‑Printed Gun, the WASP
content:
The first vibe‑coded gun is here

Gun‑rights activist and alt‑right‑friendly agitator Cody Wilson, who created the first 3D‑printed firearm 13 years ago, has announced a new device he calls the WASP, claiming it to be “the first AI‑made gun.” The weapon was displayed outside Defense Distributed headquarters in Austin, Texas, where Wilson and a sidekick clamped the WASP onto a DIY test mount while the author stood about 20 feet away.

The WASP is a 3D‑printed .22 caliber handgun that essentially consists of a pistol barrel attached to a spring‑loaded plastic box. Its rudimentary design resembles Wilson’s single‑shot 3D‑printed “Liberator,” though it incorporates additional features. The full story is available at The Verge.
summary: Cody Wilson claims the WASP is the first AI‑made 3D‑printed firearm. The WASP, a 22‑caliber handgun, was demonstrated on a DIY test mount outside Defense Distributed headquarters in Austin, Texas.

title: Sony Xperia 10 VI Won’t Receive Android 17 Update
content:
Sony has announced that the mid‑range Xperia 10 VI will not receive the Android 17 update it was originally promised. The device, launched more than two years ago with a Qualcomm Snapdragon 6 Gen 1 chipset and Android 14, had been slated for three major OS upgrades, including the current Android 17 release.

A notice posted to Sony’s UK support site explains that a detailed technical assessment found limitations related to the Xperia 10 VI’s storage configuration. These limitations mean the phone does not support an Android 17 upgrade experience that Sony considers adequate. As a result, the company has decided not to make the Android 17 upgrade available for the Xperia 10 VI.
summary: Sony promised the mid‑range Xperia 10 VI three major OS updates, including Android 17, when it launched with Android 14. A technical assessment of the device’s storage configuration led Sony to decide the phone will not support an adequate Android 17 upgrade.

title: iPhone Duo orders delayed to 2027 after Apple opens preorders
content:
Apple’s iPhone Duo pre‑orders, launched at 8 AM ET on Friday, saw delivery estimates slip into 2027 within an hour of opening. Every configuration listed on Apple’s website now shows a late‑January delivery date.

The foldable model is scheduled to hit retail stores on October 23rd, and Apple typically keeps a portion of units for in‑store availability. While online orders remain delayed, customers may obtain a device sooner by purchasing in person at an Apple Store. The extended wait could stem from high demand for Apple’s first foldable iPhone, limited supply on Apple’s side, or a combination of both.

Apple announced the iPhone Duo in September.
summary: Delivery estimates for the iPhone Duo slipped into 2027 after Apple opened preorders at 8AM ET Friday. Late January delivery dates are listed for every configuration, but the foldable is slated to launch in stores on October 23rd and some units may be available in-person at Apple Stores.

title: Ninja Labs releases MagSafe Flex Pouch, a stretchy storage pouch for phones
content:
A new accessory for smartphones that use wireless chargers and other magnetic attachments has been unveiled. The MagSafe Flex Pouch is marketed as a storage upgrade that can be attached to a phone via MagSafe.

The pouch resembles a magnetic wallet that can hold a small stack of credit cards, but its capacity extends far beyond thin plastic cards thanks to an extremely stretchy silicone design. The product is priced at $58 and is produced by Ninja Labs.

On Ninja Labs’ website the company offers a range of suggestions for using the pouch, including using it as a MagSafe wallet that can hold more items than a standard wallet. The accessory is not intended to provide additional space for apps, photos, or videos.
summary: Ninja Labs has released the MagSafe Flex Pouch, a stretchy silicone accessory that can hold more than credit cards and is compatible with wireless chargers and other magnetic accessories. The $58 pouch is marketed as a storage upgrade for smartphones and the company's website offers various usage suggestions.

content:
Veritas, the startup that has developed an anti‑counterfeit chip, is now extending its technology to jewelry, trophies and fragrance bottles. The company says the chip will help verify the authenticity of these items and protect consumers from “superfakes” that are increasingly difficult to distinguish from genuine goods.

Counterfeits of luxury goods remain a major problem for fashion houses, with counterfeiters improving their ability to replicate brands’ marks. Veritas wants to tackle the issue with its own verification chip. The company was founded by Luci Holland, a former Tesla technical.
summary: Veritas is expanding its anti-counterfeit chip to jewelry, trophies, and fragrance bottles. The startup, founded by Luci Holland, aims to verify luxury goods and fight counterfeiters who produce superfakes.

content:
A call has been issued for individuals who use artificial intelligence to aid in online dating. The request invites people to share how they have employed AI tools for chat‑up lines or social coaching while navigating the online dating world. Respondents are encouraged to describe what worked and what did not.

title: Meta launches Muse Spark Open, claims it rivals Chinese AI models
content:
Meta launched a new open‑weight AI model, Muse Spark Open, on Thursday. The company says the model is designed to compete with, and in some cases outperform, similar products from leading Chinese developers.

Meta claims Muse excels at multi‑step reasoning and complex software engineering, positioning it as a tool that could help the firm close the gap with its Chinese rivals. The announcement comes as Meta continues to expand its AI offerings.

In a post on X, Meta’s chief of AI Alexandr Wang described Muse Spark Open as “the most capable US open‑weight model to date.”
summary: Meta launched the Muse Spark Open open-weight AI model on Thursday. The model is said to excel at multi‑step reasoning and complex software engineering, and Meta claims it rivals or outperforms similar Chinese products.

title: Calls Grow to Limit London Robotaxi Rollout as Drivers Protest
content:
A protest is planned at Wayve’s headquarters as Uber drivers express concern about their future and city politicians call for Transport for London to have authority over robotaxi licences. The demonstration follows the launch of the first UK robotaxi services in September, which has sparked debate over regulation and driver security.

Passengers across Britain are eager to try the new technology, with more than 100,000 people on Uber’s London waitlist. While the service has generated enthusiasm, some view it with trepidation, reflecting uncertainty about its impact on existing transport workers.

Uber driver Florentina Ghiuzan from Essex said, “I think we should all be worried. I was shocked TfL approved it so soon. I knew change would come. But I thought it would come with a solution for us.” The protest is scheduled to take place at Wayve’s headquarters.
summary: A protest is planned at Wayve HQ as Uber drivers fear for their future and city politicians demand TfL have power over licences. More than 100,000 passengers are on Uber’s London waitlist for robotaxis, which began service in September, and driver Florentina Ghiuzan from Essex says, "I think we should all be worried" about TfL's rapid approval.

content:
The UK government will ban pornographic content that depicts strangulation and incest in England and Wales from 6 November. The new legislation will take effect early next month, outlawing the specified material.

The ban follows recommendations from a 2025 review into pornography regulation. Campaigners welcomed the legislation, noting it was prompted by cross‑party pressure that led ministers to announce new laws earlier this year.
summary: The government announced that pornography showing strangulation and incest will be illegal in England and Wales from 6 November. The ban follows a 2025 review recommendation and was welcomed by campaigners after cross‑party pressure led ministers to act earlier this year.

content:

During the presentation, the Roadster 2 drove up a curved ramp before activating SpaceX rocket thrusters that lifted the vehicle, allowing it to fly, flip and land. Musk highlighted that the sports car is equipped with thrusters and can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in less than a second.

content:

content:

content:

title: African designers spotlighted at Paris Fashion Week Spring‑Summer 2027
content:
Paris Fashion Week’s spring‑summer 2027 ready‑to‑wear collections put Africa in the spotlight. Designers highlighted the continent’s creative energy and social relevance on the global runway.

title: EU proposes Canada could become its first associate member
content:
The European Union is looking to strengthen ties with like‑minded allies as the international context becomes more challenging, and Canada is a key part of that effort.  

In her State of the Union speech in September, EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced that Canada could become an associate member of the bloc, a status that does not currently exist for any EU partner.  

If adopted, the arrangement would make Canada the EU’s first associate member.
summary: The European Union is seeking to boost ties with like‑minded allies such as Canada. In Ursula von der Leyen’s State of the Union speech in September, she announced that Canada could become an associate member, a status that does not currently exist for any EU partner.

title: Wyoming conservatives split as midterm elections near
content:
Wyoming, the nation’s least populated, most rural and most conservative state, is showing signs of division within the Republican Party just two weeks before the U.S. midterm elections. Reporters James André and Sylvain Rousseau traveled across the Cowboy State and observed a split among supporters of President Donald Trump.

The journalists’ on‑the‑ground reporting highlights that, despite Wyoming’s strong Republican reputation, the party aligned with Trump is not unified as the election approaches. This internal discord marks a notable development in a state traditionally viewed as a solid GOP stronghold.
summary: Wyoming is the least populated, most rural and most conservative state in the United States. With two weeks until the midterm elections, reporters James André and Sylvain Rousseau reported that the party of US President Donald Trump is deeply divided in the state.
author: France 24

title: French MEP Bernard Guetta calls Donald Trump a liar and says US not ally to Ukraine
content:
French MEP Bernard Guetta, a veteran French journalist and member of the European Parliament for the centrist Renew group, criticized the current U.S. president in a recent interview. Guetta called Donald Trump a liar, arguing that Trump had told the American public that Zelensky and the Ukrainian resistance were responsible for the rise in diesel prices, a claim Guetta described as a pure lie.

He further accused Trump of being responsible for starting a war with Iran. Guetta also warned that without American intelligence sharing, Ukraine is becoming weaker, and he condemned the U.S. president’s perceived support for Putin against Ukraine.
summary: French journalist and commentator Bernard Guetta, a Member of the European Parliament for the centrist Renew group, called Donald Trump a liar who blamed Zelensky and the Ukrainian resistance for diesel prices and said Trump was responsible for starting a war with Iran. He said that without American intelligence sharing Ukraine is weaker and accused the U.S. president of giving a hand to Putin against Ukraine.
author: France 24

title: Pope Leo XIV celebrates mass at Rome's Gemelli hospital after lung cancer surgery
content:
Pope Leo XIV celebrated a mass at Rome’s Gemelli hospital on Friday after undergoing surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung. Photos released by the Vatican showed the pontiff leading the service in the hospital chapel.  

Doctors reported that his recovery was progressing normally. They said further tests would determine whether the cancer had spread.
summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated mass at Rome's Gemelli hospital on Friday after surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung. Doctors said his recovery was progressing normally but further tests would show whether the cancer had spread.
author: France 24

title: Ethiopia Appoints Interim Government in Tigray Ahead of Elections
content:
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced on Friday the formation of an interim administration for the northern Tigray region. The interim government is tasked with preparing elections that the prime minister says will be held within six months.

The region had been under the control of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front, which has been in conflict with government forces since September. The renewed fighting revived a war that, between 2020 and 2022, resulted in the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people.
summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced the appointment of an interim administration in the northern Tigray region, which had been controlled by the Tigray People's Liberation Front and has clashed with government forces since September, and the administration will prepare for elections within six months. The recent conflict revived a war that killed hundreds of thousands between 2020 and 2022.
author: France 24

title: South African Lions player found dead in French hotel before Champions Cup match
content:
A South African rugby player for the Lions team was found dead at a hotel in France on Friday, the eve of the club’s European Champions Cup match against La Rochelle. Local media reported the fatal discovery, but the player’s identity has not yet been released.

The incident occurred just before the Lions’ debut in the Champions Cup, and no further details have been made public.
summary: A South African rugby player for the Lions was found dead at a hotel in France on Friday. The death occurred on the eve of the team's European Champions Cup game against La Rochelle, and the player's identity has not been released.

title: Italy cuts air traffic in half due to data transmission problems
content:
Italian authorities have halved the number of flights in the country’s airspace, citing problems with the data transmission network. The reduction follows an assessment by the ENAV authority that the issue was not caused by malicious activity.

ENAV confirmed that, despite the network trouble, flights remain safe. The authority’s statement emphasized that safety is being maintained while the data transmission problem is addressed.
summary: Italian authorities have cut air traffic in half due to problems with the data transmission network. The ENAV authority ruled out malicious activity and said flights remained safe.

title: Kenya reports first two confirmed Ebola cases, ministry urges calm
content:
Kenya has confirmed its first two Ebola cases, a development that has prompted urgent questions about the country’s public health preparedness and border control measures. The cases have sparked concern among health officials and the public regarding the nation's capacity to manage a potential outbreak.

In response, the health ministry has stated that there is no need for panic, indicating that authorities are monitoring the situation closely.
summary: Kenya has confirmed its first two Ebola cases, prompting urgent questions about the country's public health preparedness and border controls. The health ministry said there is no need for panic.

title: EU aims to boost economy with AI while safeguarding workers, safety and climate
content:
The European Union is looking to accelerate its economy through artificial intelligence, aiming to keep pace with the United States and China.  

The EU’s strategy raises questions about whether it can compete globally while also safeguarding workers, ensuring safety, and protecting the climate.
summary: The European Union is seeking to boost its economy with artificial intelligence. It aims to do so while protecting workers, safety and the climate.

title: Jamaican filmmakers use Sky's Possession to confront enslavement and colonial trauma
content:
Sky’s supernatural series Possession opens with a woman releasing a violent spirit from a 300‑year‑old box, a visual metaphor for colonialism and oppression returning to the surface. The scene has been highlighted by observers as emblematic of a broader shift in Jamaica’s film industry, where creators are increasingly using the island’s landscape to tell stories that confront enslavement, trauma and historical memory.

The series follows a biracial British lawyer who travels to Jamaica to investigate a multimillion‑pound inheritance dispute, only to uncover a dark, vengeful spirit linked to the plantation’s brutal colonial past. Critics describe the work as a form of “cultural reparation,” with confident Jamaican creatives reclaiming the island’s narratives on screen.
summary: Sky's supernatural series Possession shows a woman opening a 300‑year‑old box that releases a spirit symbolising colonialism and oppression. The show illustrates a shift in Jamaica’s film industry as directors employ the landscape to tell stories confronting enslavement, trauma and historical memory.

content:
Patients were rescued from a suspected illegal rehabilitation centre in South Africa where they had been kept in chains.  

Authorities reported that about 200 patients were taken from the facility, which was described as overcrowded.  

Officials noted that some of the individuals had “sores all over their bodies” when they were found.
summary: Patients were rescued from a suspected illegal rehab centre in South Africa where they had been kept in chains. Some of the 200 patients were found with sores covering their bodies and housed in overcrowded rooms.

content:

The senators’ call for inquiry follows Kyiv’s claim that the reduced bandwidth hampered its military operations.
summary: US senators have called for an investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions. Ukraine says temporary speed limits on the Starlink internet network disrupted its battlefield missions.

title: Joshua Foster fined after 2‑year‑old son dies in Cyprus hotel window fall
content:
A father was fined after his two‑year‑old son died in a fall at a hotel in Cyprus.  

Joshua Foster lost control of his son while showing him the view of a water park from a window, an incident that resulted in the child’s death.  

Foster was subsequently issued a fine for the incident.
summary: Joshua Foster was fined after his 2‑year‑old son died in a fall from a hotel window in Cyprus. Foster said he lost control of his son while showing him the view of a water park from the window.

content: Australia’s women’s Rugby League World Cup opener began today in Sydney, with the Jillaroos facing Fetu Samoa. The match kicked off with Australia already underway. During the anthem, several Samoan players were seen tearing up, a moment highlighted as special for them to represent their country on the world stage.

title: Opta analysis questions if Premier League teams must run more to win
content:
Pundits frequently criticize Premier League teams for insufficient running, prompting a question about whether distance covered correlates with match results. Following Manchester United’s loss of points against Tottenham, commentators questioned the Red Devils’ effort, citing physical statistics to support their critique.

Jamie Redknapp, speaking on Sky Sports, noted a recurring pattern where teams that run more than their opponents tend to succeed. He described running more than the opposition as a “non-negotiable” in the current Premier League, stating that teams must either cover more distance or stay close enough to make it irrelevant. Redknapp specifically highlighted that Tottenham ran five kilometers more than Manchester United in that match.
summary: Pundits often criticize teams for insufficient running, with Jamie Redknapp citing Tottenham's five-kilometer advantage over Manchester United. An Opta analyst examines whether a direct link exists between distance covered and match results.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Auctioneer David Convery Drives 332‑Lot Budds Sale, £700 Barclays Trophy Sold
content:
David Convery, an auctioneer with three decades of experience, recently led a sale of 332 lots at Budds auction house, an event he described as an “Octoberfest” of sporting memorabilia. During the auction, a Barclays Manager of the Month trophy, complete with a travel case but without an identified owner, sold for £700, exceeding its estimate. Convery is noted for having secured world-record prices in the past, including for the oldest surviving FA Cup and Pelé’s 1970 World Cup final shirt.

The article by Emma John frames this market as a marker of sport’s “rampant self-inflation,” comparable to rising transfer fees and ticket prices. The piece highlights the commercial scale of the industry, featuring items ranging from historic trophies to player memorabilia, such as the shorts associated with Eric Cantona mentioned in the title.
summary: Auctioneer David Convery led a Budds auction featuring 332 lots, including a Barclays Manager of the Month trophy that sold for £700. Convery, who has auctioned world‑record items such as the oldest FA Cup and Pelé’s 1970 World Cup shirt, has managed twice as many lots in other sales.

content:

content:

content: Sonay Kartal upset fifth seed Elina Svitolina in the quarter‑finals of the Wuhan Open, extending her winning streak after a long injury lay‑off and securing a spot in the tournament’s semi‑finals. content:

Hurzeler’s career began in Germany, where he coached at the fifth‑tier level before moving to England to take charge of Brighton.

content:

summary: The Premier League has had a defined 'Big Six' consisting of Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur. The article questions whether this era is coming to an end.

title: Olympic sprinter Beth Dobbin now largely bedbound after ME diagnosis
content:
Beth Dobbin, who represented Great Britain as a sprinter at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, is now largely bedbound. She has been diagnosed with myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME), a debilitating illness that currently has no cure.

The condition has left Dobbin confined to bed for 22 hours a day, marking a stark contrast to her former athletic career.
summary: Beth Dobbin, who represented Great Britain in the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, is now largely bedbound. She was diagnosed with ME, a disease that has no cure.

The case could ultimately be heard by the Supreme Court, which is described as conservative‑leaning.

title: Antibiotic Resistance in Nairobi Gut Bacteria Displaces Healthy Microbes
content:
Good gut bacteria vs. bad: What we learned about antibiotic resistance from a community in Nairobi

Years of antibiotic use have fueled a rise in bacteria that can survive antibiotics. In a Nairobi community, these antibiotic‑resistant bacteria are competing with and displacing other bacteria that are naturally present in the human gut, where they play a critical role in maintaining good health.

The displacement of natural gut bacteria by resistant strains has led to increased illness and death from diseases that were once easily treatable with antibiotics.
summary: Years of antibiotic use in a Nairobi community have fueled a rise in bacteria that survive antibiotics. These resistant bacteria compete with and displace natural gut bacteria, leading to increased illness and death from diseases once easily treatable with antibiotics.

title: Depression treatment during pregnancy linked to infant brain development, study finds
content:
A new randomized trial reported in Nature Communications indicates that treating depression during pregnancy can affect infant brain development and early emotional function.  

The study found that maternal depression treatment influences the developing brain of the baby and its subsequent emotional outcomes, suggesting potential benefits of addressing depression while pregnant.
summary: Treating depression during pregnancy influences infant brain development and early emotional function. The research was published in Nature Communications.

title: New Perspective Explores Why Pressure Can Cause Failure or Peak Performance
content: High-stakes scenarios, such as a decisive penalty kick in a final, match point in tennis, or the last attempt in a competition, often cause well-practiced performances to break down when significant outcomes are at stake. However, pressure does not always impair performance, as some individuals achieve their best results precisely during these critical moments. Existing explanations for these varying reactions to pressure are only partial.
summary: When a lot is at stake, even a well-practiced performance can suddenly break down. Yet some people perform at their best precisely in the moments that matter most.

title: Future Arctic winter sea ice loss likely underestimated, study finds
content:
Future Arctic winter sea ice is projected to shrink by roughly 1 million square kilometers (386,000 square miles) more than earlier estimates suggested.  

The new estimate comes after researchers examined clues from a warm period that occurred about 6,000 years ago. By incorporating these ancient data into climate models, they improved the models’ reliability for predicting sea‑ice changes.  

The updated projections indicate a larger loss of winter sea ice in the Arctic than previously thought.
summary: Researchers used clues from a warm period 6,000 years ago to improve climate model reliability. The improved models indicate future Arctic winter sea ice could shrink about 1 million square kilometers more than previously thought.

content: AI has made significant advances in computer programming and mathematics, prompting speculation that physics could be the next field to experience a similar transformation. summary: AI has taken huge strides in computer programming and mathematics. Physics could be the next field to be turned upside down by AI.

title: Egypt's climate‑resilient “super corals” in Red Sea begin showing heat stress
content:
Egypt’s Red Sea reefs, dubbed “super corals” for their historic resistance to bleaching, are now showing signs of heat stress. Scientists note that these corals have long been immune to bleaching, a phenomenon that has puzzled researchers.

Researchers remain divided over the reasons behind this resilience, but they agree that understanding the underlying mechanisms could be crucial for protecting the corals as climate change begins to take its toll.
summary: Scientists cannot agree why Red Sea reefs have long been immune to bleaching. They hope that uncovering the reason could help protect the resilient corals as climate change takes its toll.

content:
Benchmark, a Silicon Valley venture‑capital firm, warned that the industry’s informal agreement not to back rival startups is weakening. The firm said the “rule against backing rivals” is becoming “harder to keep,” attributing the shift to the rise of artificial‑intelligence technologies.  

Benchmark’s observation highlights growing pressure on venture firms to invest across competing AI‑driven companies, challenging a long‑standing pact in the Valley.

content:

title: Turkey's worst rainfall in 80 years causes deadly floods near Istanbul
content:
Heavy rain, described as the worst in eight decades, has caused severe flooding in areas surrounding Istanbul, Turkey. The torrential downpour turned streets into rivers, overturning vehicles and cutting off power supplies.

Emergency crews are working to clear the wreckage, but the disaster has already claimed at least three lives and left five people missing.

title: Syria arrests Ali Kayali, accused of 2013 Bayda and Baniyas civilian killings
content:
Syria announced the arrest of Ali Kayali, a 70‑year‑old militia commander known as “Mihrac Ural.” The security operation targets the individual accused of leading al‑Assad‑affiliated forces that carried out mass killings along the coast.

According to authorities, Kayali’s militia conducted summary executions of more than 450 civilians in the towns of Bayda and Baniyas during May 2013. The arrests come as part of ongoing efforts to hold those responsible for the 2013 coastal massacres accountable.
summary: Syria arrested 70‑year‑old Ali Kayali, also known as Mihrac Ural. He commanded al‑Assad‑affiliated militia forces that carried out summary executions of more than 450 civilians in Bayda and Baniyas in May 2013.

content:

The projected price rise and revenue target are part of the same fiscal plan aimed at strengthening the country's tax base.
summary: Germany plans to increase its tobacco tax, which could push the price of a pack of cigarettes to close to €12 by 2030. The government expects the tax hike to raise an additional €12 billion over four years.

content:

The demand for accountability follows the deaths of the 34 children in the incident.

content:

Developed by SkyFall, the unmanned aircraft is called StarGate and is designed to carry a wounded soldier inside an enclosed cabin. The drone’s capacity to transport a person marks a departure from conventional medical evacuation methods.

The demonstration was filmed showing StarGate taking off, flying and landing with a person on board, illustrating its operational capabilities for rapid rescue missions.
summary: SkyFall demonstrated a battlefield rescue system featuring a drone that can carry a wounded soldier inside an enclosed cabin. The drone, named StarGate, was filmed taking off, flying and landing with a person on board.
